newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks off lows, sector performances vary.
newsitem.headline: French stocks off lows, sector performances vary.

text.p: French stocks were off their lows at midday on Monday as investors anticipated a new Socialist-led government would not adopt radically market-unfriendly policies, brokers said.

But the performance varied by sector, with stocks involved in privatisations and restructurings suffering far more than the market as a whole. In contrast, shares in dollar earners, consumer goods companies and retailers outperformed.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 1.64 percent at 2,541.60 points at 0947 GMT, well off its early low of 2,498.75. The CAC-40 June futures contract was down 47 points at 2,520.
Volume was a very heavy 4.83 billion francs.
Although the final results showing the Communists will hold the balance of power in a Socialist-led government was the least attractive scenario for the markets, investors are staying cool.

"People aren't that scared," one trader said. "They can't raise taxes. The right already did that. They can make life miserable for companies trying to restructure but they can't stop that. They'll do symbolic things."
Caution is expected to prevail, however, ahead of the full impact this afternoon of foreign investor reaction.
Volatility is also expected "when they start speaking," a broker said, referring to the new government.
* Privatisation shares including Lagardere, Thomson-CSF worst hit. Dassault Aviation suspended limit-down.
* Banking, financial and auto shares weak on concerns that restructurings involving redundancies could be blocked or delayed.
